Observation: - James Dean: James Byron Dean (February 8, 1931 – September 30, 1955) was an American actor. He is remembered as a cultural icon of teenage disillusionment and social estrangement, as expressed in the title of his most celebrated film, "Rebel Without a Cause" (1955), in which he starred as troubled teenager Jim Stark. The other two films in his short but impactful career were "East of Eden" (1955) and "Giant" (1956). Dean's premature death in a car crash at age 24 cemented his legendary status. He became the first actor to receive a posthumous Academy Award nomination for Best Actor for his role as Cal Trask in "East of Eden", and received a second posthumous nomination for his role as Jett Rink in "Giant".
